title: A sheaf supported in low dimension is a filtered union
statement:
Let $B$ be a finite-type
scheme over a field $K$. Suppose a torsion
etale sheaf $N$ has zero
geometric stalk at every point $y$ with
$\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(y)>a$, where $a\geq0$.
For each closed $Z\subset B$ of dimension at most $a$, let
$j_Z:B\setminus Z\to B$ and set
$N_Z=\ker(N\to j_{Z*}j_Z^*N)$.
Then the canonical map $\varinjlim_Z N_Z\to N$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Let I be the set of closed subsets $Z\subseteq |B|$ of dimension at most $a$, ordered by inclusion. It is small, since it is a subset of the power set of $|B|$, and nonempty, since it contains the empty set. If $Z_1,Z_2\in I$, an irreducible closed subset of $Z_1\cup Z_2$ lies in one of them: intersect with each closed set and use irreducibility. Any strict chain in the union consequently lies wholly in the set containing its largest member. Thus $\dim(Z_1\cup Z_2)\leq a$, and I is directed.

source.place: Proof, first sentence; expanded chain argument

proof.text: For an open inclusion $j:U\to B$, $j^*N$ is the restriction of N to etale objects over U. Indeed this restriction is left adjoint to $j_*$: a map on U gives on each V over B the map $N(V)\to N(V\times_B U)\to F(V\times_B U)$; conversely restrict a map $N\to j_*F$ to objects over U. On an object over U its base change to U is itself, so restriction of the first construction recovers the original map. Conversely, naturality of a map $N\to j_*F$ along $V\times_B U\to V$ says that its component at V equals its component at $V\times_B U$ composed with the restriction of N, since the restriction of $j_*F$ along this arrow is the identity after the canonical identifications. Thus the second construction followed by the first recovers that map. Both constructions commute with restriction arrows, hence are natural. The definitions of inverse and direct image therefore identify the unit on V with restriction to $V\times_B U$. Consequently $N_Z(V)=\{s\in N(V):s|_{V\times_B(B\setminus Z)}=0\}$. This is a subsheaf (local zero restrictions glue), its inclusion in N is monic, and $Z\subseteq Z'$ gives the inclusion $N_Z\subseteq N_{Z'}$, with the required cocone to N.

source.place: Proof, definition of N_Z and last sentence; explicit adjunction calculation

proof.text: Represent a geometric germ by a section on a pointed affine etale neighbourhood V, using affine cofinality. The composite V to B to Spec K is locally of finite type. Therefore V is locally Noetherian; since V is affine it is also quasi-compact, hence Noetherian. This uses only the locally Noetherian conclusion of LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian, not a quasi-compactness assertion for V to B or a finite-type neighbourhood refinement.

source.place: Proof, take a section on a finite-type etale V; affine refinement for stalk representatives

proof.text: Apply the zero-locus lemma to the section on V. Let W be its zero open and S the closed complement of W. A point v in S cannot have image residue-field transcendence degree greater than a: take the algebraic closure of the residue field of V at v and compose its geometric point with V to B. The hypothesis makes its stalk zero, and the zero-locus lemma then factors this lift through W, contradicting v in S. Since V is Noetherian, S has a finite cover by irreducible closed subsets, each with a generic point by sobriety. If S is empty the cover may be empty.

Write $p:V\to B$ and $y_i=p(v_i)$. Choose a geometric lift of $v_i$; its nonzero germ is in $N_{\bar y_i}$ by the zero-locus lemma. The hypothesis forces $\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa_B(y_i)\leq a$. Put $C_i=\overline{\{y_i\}}\subseteq B$. This is an irreducible closed subset with generic point y_i. Its dimension is at most a by the generic-residue-field dimension lemma. Moreover $p(S_i)\subseteq C_i$: continuity sends every specialization of v_i to a specialization of y_i. Since y_i itself is in p(S_i), its image closure is exactly C_i. Set $Z=\bigcup_i C_i$. This is closed and has dimension at most a by the finite-union chain argument of step 1; it contains p(S). When r=0 set Z empty. This implements the blueprint image-closure argument directly at the image generic points, without a residue-field degree comparison.

source.place: Proof, generic-point hypothesis and closure of image of S; dimension input Stacks 0B1C

proof.text: Every etale arrow into V whose composite image in B avoids Z has image in W, hence kills the section by the zero-locus lemma. Calculate the open-immersion adjunction unit using the site-level map/pullback adjunction and the canonical isomorphism between upperStar and localization restriction. Its component at V is therefore zero on the section. Evaluation of a sheaf kernel at V is a kernel of abelian groups, so the section lifts to D(Z)(V). Naturality of the germ maps gives a lift of the original germ along the stalk map of c.app Z. Thus the support-kernel stalks exhaust every stalk at a residue-field algebraic-closure point.

Each c.app Z is monic because its specified fork is a kernel. Abelian etale sheaves form a Grothendieck abelian category, so filtered colimits preserve monomorphisms. Apply this to c from D to the constant diagram at N; the latter has colimit N because the nonempty filtered index is connected. Hence the colimit comparison is monic. To prove it epic, take maps g,h from N which agree after that comparison. They agree after every c.app Z. Every element of every residue-field algebraic-closure stalk of N lifts along one of these maps by step 6; consequently the stalk maps of g and h agree. Geometric-stalk faithfulness implies g=h, giving epimorphicity. A mono and epi in an abelian category is an isomorphism. No stalk-colimit preservation or stalk exactness is needed. The torsion hypothesis is retained unchanged but unused.

source.place: Lemma 03CO (filtered colimits are exact), combined with the blueprint section-support argument and geometric-stalk faithfulness

proof_origin.place: Proof, implemented with affine locally Noetherian neighbourhoods and the Grothendieck-abelian filtered-colimit argument; existing zero-open and dimension/trdeg lemmas retained

The natural transformation c, its zero-composite condition hz and kernel universal property hk specify precisely N_Z with its inclusion into N; naturality forces the canonical transition maps. This avoids a separate definition for the diagram and is invariant under the unique compatible isomorphisms between choices of kernels.
